articles.title: RAF Abu Dhabi Featuring Khamzat Chimaev and Merab Dvalishvili Live Updates, Highlights, Results
articles.summary: Saturday's star-studded RAF Abu Dhabi card provide some solid entertainment for the combat sports that decided to tune in.
articles.body:
Chris Weidman gave a pretty good account of himself against the much younger Khamzat Chimaev in the RAF Abu Dhabi main event, but ultimately lost by tech fall (10-0).

With the win, Chimaev defends the RAF light heavyweight crossover title. He's now 5-0 on the RAF mats, with other over Robbie Lawler, Tyron Woodley, Dillon Danis, and Gilbert Burns.

"It feels amazing," he said in his post-match interview with Chael Sonnen.

"Anyone who wants to fight, wrestle, grapple, whatever," he added when asked what's next. "I'm always ready."

articles.title: AEW Full Gear 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of AEW Full Gear 2026 from Phoenix Arizona.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of AEW Full Gear 2026 from Phoenix Arizona.

This year's event is serving as a bit of an unofficial tribute show for Pac due to the name of the show being born from a joke made during a BTE segment.

As usual, AEW packed the card with title bouts, stipulations, grudge matches and all of the major players currently in storylines.

Let's take a look at what went down at this year's show.

Here is the lineup from this year's Full Gear PPV.

Queen Aminata vs. Persephone vs. Hyan vs. Skye Blue (TBS Championship)

The Brawling Birds vs. Wrathlander (Women's Tag Team Championships)

The Young Bucks vs. Mark Davis and Jake Doyle (Men's Tag Team Championships)

Brodido and Adam Page vs. The New Level and Swerve Strickland (Trios Championships)

The Death Riders vs. The Cut (Anarchy in the Arena)

Kazuchika Okada vs. Adam Copeland (International Championship)

Tommaso Ciampa vs. Ilja Dragunov (National Championship)

Marina Shafir vs. Mercedes Mone (Women's World Championship)

Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher (AEW World Heavyweight Championship)

The first match on the pre-show saw Jack Perry Battle The Beast Mortos. There was no real story behind this match, so it was just two guys fighting to get a win at a major event, and sometimes that is all you need.

This was a solid match. It was good, but not in a way that is going to outshine what is set to come, so it was a nice way to get the crowd into the right mood without the show peaking too early. Perry sent a message to Samoa Joe by hitting Mortos with a Muscle Buster to get the win.

Wardlow, Kevin Knight and El Clon vs. Local Talents

Three members of the Don Callis Family were in action against three local talents. As you could probably assume from that description, this was not a very long fight.

Each member of the DCF had a chance to be in the ring for a few moments to hit some moves. It was over within a couple of minutes, with Knight scoring the pin for his team.

The next match kept the DCF at ringside with Rocky Romero, Trent Beretta, Lance Archer and Josh Alexander taking on Darius Martin, Matt Sydal, QT Marshall and Big Boom AJ, the Costco guy.

This was a little more exciting than the usual Costco Guys match, but it was still kind of gimmicky and felt like a random excuse to throw a bunch of people together. Boom and Doom continued to be undefeated after getting the win.

Result: Boom and Doom, Martin and Sydal won

Queen Aminata vs. Persephone vs. Hyan vs. Skye Blue

The only match on the pre-show that really mattered ended the Tailgate Brawl with Aminata defending her TBS title against Persephone, Hyan and Skye Blue. The original plan was a triple threat with Maya World, but travel issues forced a change to the card.

This was high-energy right out of the gate. All four women were giving it their all and delivered a fun performance. This easily outshone everything else on the pre-show. Aminata was able to get the win to retain her title.

Before the show, AEW revealed that the trios titles now contain a tribute to Pac on the leather straps.

Perry has added a little bit of size to his physique. It's not much, but enough to be visibly noticeable.

One of the jobbers had some trouble getting up for the powerbomb.

The Rizzler and Big Justice were not at ringside.

The way Blue took a chair to the face looked brutal.

Kazuchika Okada vs. Adam Copeland (International Title)

The first match on the main card saw Copeland challenge Okada for the International Championship. This is one of those matches that seemed impossible for a long time, so a lot of fans were excited to see two veterans have their first singles match ever.

The Rainmaker was the first to get the upper hand after playing his usual mind games, but Cope did not let him keep it for long. He made Okada leave the ring to take a breather after almost hitting a Spear very early.

The champion exposed part of the concrete floor and attempted a piledriver, but he was unsuccessful. It ended up coming back into play later when Okada hit an Impaler on the floor.

This match had a steady pace and was structured more in sequences than as one continuous fight. They would pick up the pace, hit a big move, and then slow down again for a bit. It's a tried-and-true formula that many matches have used.

Okada and Copeland had very different careers leading to this point, and have worked in very different styles, but being the pros that they are, they had zero issues finding their groove and giving us a fun show.

The Rated-R Superstar put up a good fight, but The Rainmaker got the win to retain his title.

Okada's entrance gear was a little more ornate than usual.

Cope hit an atomic drop onto a steel chair. It did not look like it would be very painful, but Okada sold it well.

There were some very anti-Don Callis fans near the ring.

Okada received a small cut on his arm after being sent into the ring post, but it did not bleed much.

The Young Bucks vs. Davis and Doyle (Men's Tag Team Titles)

Nick and Matt Jackson put their tag titles on the line against the two men who absolutely destroyed them in their last meeting, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle.

Much like in their previous encounter, the two powerhouses took control immediately. They brought the Bucks out of the ring and punished them against various parts of the set, and it looked like they might get a squash win again.

Unfortunately for the DCF, the Bucks put up more of a fight this time. Davis and Doyle still felt dominant, especially in the early minutes, but it wasn't quite as one-sided as it was last time.

Seeing Davis and Doyle finally being portrayed as a dominant force has been fantastic to watch. They feel unique in the landscape of AEW while simultaneously feeling like a throwback to tag teams of the past.

Once the Bucks started to mount some real offense, things really picked up. Their high-flying style was the perfect contrast to the powerhouse style used by their opponents, so there was a nice variety of offense throughout the match.

This match exceeded all expectations, and people were already expecting it to be good. The only thing that would have made this better was a title change, but the Bucks retained after a stellar performance from all four competitors.

The Motor City Machine Guns came out after the match since they are next in line for a title shot. They helped the Bucks up and hugged them before helping them celebrate their win, and that is when The Kasper Brothers, formerly known as The Creeds in WWE, made their debut.

They attacked and took out all four men before FTR came out. It looked like they might fight the newcomers, but they ended up joining forces, so it looks like Stokely Hathaway has some new clients that he used to manage in The Diamond Mine in NXT.

Result: The Young Bucks defeated Davis and Doyle

Unlike during Okada vs. Cope, Don Callis joined the commentary team for this one.

If you watched mid-90s WCW, Davis and Doyle are giving big Men at Work vibes, and we mean that as a compliment.

The way Nick helped Matt get Davis into position for the Meltzer Driver was creative.

The bump Nick took on the timekeeper's table looked nasty.

articles.title: Stephen Thompson Reflects On Retirement Before Last UFC Fight
articles.summary: Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson talks about what led him to call it a career ahead of his final UFC fight against Charles Radtke.
articles.body:
10-year UFC veteran Stephen Thompson is calling it a career after his fight with Charles Radtke at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden.

After a historic run in the promotion, the 43-year-old Wonderboy will step into the Octagon for a final time against a young competitor. When asked what brought him to the decision, Thompson told Forbes that recovery started getting difficult with age. Additionally, the birth of his daughter urged him to step away from MMA.

"My body does not recover like it used to," Thompson shared. "After my last fight, I went back to training and jacked my neck up; I hurt my lower back, and my knee started hurting. I had to slow down, back off on the hard training, and my body started to feel better."

"I realized I don't have a lot of time to be in the UFC, competing against these young studs. But not only that, I have a baby girl; she's five months, and that definitely changes your mindset as well," he added.

"I wanna have my body nice and healthy; five, ten, fifteen years from now, we can go hiking, riding bikes, and I won't be too banged up. That does change your mind, but when your body knows, it's time."

The kickboxing savant made his professional MMA debut at 26 after a successful amateur career.

Following a 5-0 start, Wonderboy joined the UFC in 2012. He went on to win eight of his nine fights, including four knockouts, in the promotion before a stalemate with Tyron Woodley in his first title challenge. The pair met again, but the decision favored Woodley in the rematch.

Thompson has since been 4-7 and heads into UFC 334 on a three-fight skid despite wins against impressive competition in Jorge Masvidal, Vicente Luque, and Kevin Holland. His three latest defeats came at the hands of top fighters in Gabriel Bonfim, Joaquin Buckley, and Shavkat Rakhmonov.

With the likes of Amanda Nunes, Henry Cejudo and Georges St-Pierre returning from initial retirements, Thompson is not closing the door to competing in other disciplines.

"My competitive itch is still there, but I think I'm done with MMA," he said. "I'm a striker at heart, so maybe I'll do some boxing in the future. But we'll see what that holds when she gets a little older."

"Your body knows when it's done, and you gotta accept it. You sit down with your coaches and family. I'm very close with my training partners, and I thought it's time. It was heartbreaking, and I don't know what emotions are gonna be on fight night. I may start bawling, but my main focus is getting ready."

Facing Thompson on his swansong is 36-year-old Charles Radtke, who is riding a two-fight win streak. The 12-5 fighter joined the UFC in 2023 and is 5-2 in the promotion.

When asked about his opponent, Wonderboy raved about the type of fight Radtke presents.

"He's coming at you," he said. "That's what made me want this fight. He's a battle-worn guy; he likes to put on a show, good boxing, good takedowns. I'm ready wherever the fight goes. He brings it, and that's the kind of show we want to put on at Madison Square Garden."

Wonderboy is no stranger to the bright lights at the World's Most Famous Arena. After the draw with Woodley, Thompson fought twice more at the Garden, tallying wins over Masvidal and Luque.

"Having spent some time in the Empire State, Thompson marveled at the chance to end his career with another win at Madison Square Garden."

"It's epic. To be able to go out there, New York is my home away from home," he shared. "I spent a lot of time on Long Island with Chris Weidman, Matt Serra and Ray Longo, and I fought here four times. This is my jam."

"To be able to go out with a dub for my fans here in MSG in New York City would be epic."

Apart from his entertaining fight style, Wonderboy became beloved by fans for being one of the kindest people in a dangerous sport. A victory on Saturday would elevate him to a 17-9-1 record before laying the gloves down.

"I wanna be remembered as one of the best strikers to step out in the Octagon," Thompson shared. "One of the best martial artists and just a good dude. Just a kind guy. You don't have to have a crazy persona to make it in the UFC. Being yourself is sometimes the best route and is a breath of fresh air."

articles.title: Diego Pacheco vs Darius Fulghum: Live blog, round-by-round and results
articles.summary: Diego Pacheco faces Darius Fulghum in a super middleweight main event!
articles.body:
Diego Pacheco will return to action tonight as the super middleweight contender faces Darius Fulghum in a Matchroom Boxing main event from Carson, California.

It's the second straight fight at the venue for Pacheco (26-0, 19 KO), who stopped Immanuwel Aleem in this building back in July. He now looks to close his year in the ring with a win over Fulghum (15-1-1, 13 KO), who has sort of learned on the job as a pro and hit some speed bumps in the last year and a half, but is coming off of a May win.

The show will also feature Anthony Olascuaga defending his WBO flyweight title against Yuberjen Martinez , a skilled former Olympic silver medalist who may have more upset potential than expected.

Wil Esco will be on the call tonight, leading the live blog and the round-by-round for the main event, with results and updates for the rest of the card. Join us!

David Adeleye vs Alexander Flores, heavyweights, 10 rounds

Absolute waste of time fight, if I'm being honest. We're about halfway through a fight with one fighter who isn't in there to win and Adeleye has yet to find the formula to finish the fight.

Flores goes down in the third on a hard jab.

Flores visibly scared of Adeleye from the opening bell, extremely tentative, defensive, and looking to disengage more than otherwise.

Location: Dignity Health Sports Park – Carson, CA, USA
